clue.text: European secretary's first son at Westminster?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the head of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: SW1 is the London postcode of Westminster, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
opening letter of secretary
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a European minister's eldest boy has a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the postcode trick: SW1 is Westminster's London postcode, and the 1 is read as I. The postcode comes first, then the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss is a native of Switzerland, a country in Europe, so the noun works as a synonym.

clue.text: Forager from South Carolina, one getting his own back

blocks.note: SC is the postal abbreviation of the US state South Carolina
someone who takes revenge

explanation.surface: A man from the Carolinas who scrounges for food is also out for revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger searches for and collects scraps of food or discarded things, which is what a forager does.

clue.text: Man possibly digesting core of dietary fibre

indicators.note: something being digested is taken inside, so one piece swallows the other
the core of a word is its central letter, so only the middle is kept

blocks.note: the Isle of Man is one example of an isle
the central letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man possibly' is not a person but the Isle of Man; 'possibly' says it is just one example of an isle. 'Dietary fibre' is the surface phrase, but the definition is fibre alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre from Mexican agave and yucca, used for cordage and brushes.

clue.text: Interval in which Jew possibly receives cricket side

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece holds the other within it

explanation.surface: A break in play during which a Jewish player welcomes a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on side; ON is a staple crossword abbreviation for that half.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest musical interval in Western music, half a whole tone.

clue.text: Distressing start to period in university environment

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
one piece is placed inside what follows, sitting within the other letters

blocks.note: first letter of period
U is the standard abbreviation for university
a setting is the surroundings or environment

explanation.surface: A troubling beginning to term on a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes inside the combined 'university environment', slotting between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsetting is an adjective meaning causing worry or unhappiness, so it is a synonym of distressing.

clue.text: In part Louis toured a Hebridean island or two

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, so the letters sit within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, inside the first and into the second

explanation.surface: A man called Louis visited parts of the Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or two' is fair because there are two islands of the name, North Uist and South Uist, in the Outer Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Uist is the name of islands in the Outer Hebrides, a chain off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Skill in mounting shows — HMS Pinafore, for example?

blocks.note: first meaning: the theatrical skill of staging productions
second meaning: a ship that exists only on the stage

explanation.surface: A theatrical skill illustrated by the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta HMS Pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera set aboard a naval ship; the question mark warns that read as two words the answer is a vessel on a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecraft is expertise in theatre production, and split up it names a boat built for the theatre, which the operetta's ship is.

clue.text: Uproar surrounding extremely large Spanish city

the two end letters of large

explanation.walkthrough: 'Large Spanish city' reads as one phrase, but 'extremely large' is the wordplay and only 'Spanish city' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, the old capital of Castile.

clue.text: Good woman in fashionable church: a blissful state for some

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed inside the later ones

explanation.walkthrough: The definition draws on the saying 'ignorance is bliss', hence 'for some'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'ignorance is bliss' says not knowing can be a happy condition, which the definition alludes to.

clue.text: Maxim, a banker in Zurich?

explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is an aphorism, and the phrase 'gnomes of Zurich' gave the word a sense of a shadowy Swiss financier.

clue.text: Site Maria prepared for a herbaceous plant

clue.text: Key openings for items in sports programme

blocks.note: E is a musical key
vents are openings or outlets

clue.text: Policeman needing information runs in titled lady

clue.text: Possible battle with fussy kid over veg at duke's grassland?

blocks.clueFragment: Possible battle with fussy kid over veg

clue.text: Government department's former auditor mentioned in speech

explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department in charge of public revenue, headed by the Chancellor.

clue.text: A set of books one is opposed to?

I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is a person who dislikes a library set against reading?
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning against, so it can stand in for opposed to.

clue.text: Crossed Bury, needing basic food picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
bread is a staple food

explanation.surface: Someone from the Lancashire town of Bury is cross because they need basic groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, capitalised, poses as the Lancashire town, but it is the verb. 'Crossed' is the breeding sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals or plants that interbred have mated across breeds or species, so they were crossed.

clue.text: Cross-examining cook over misplaced gin

the three letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Grilling someone is questioning them intensely, as in a hostile interrogation.

clue.text: People in the Tour de France, for example

blocks.clueFragment: the Tour de France, for example
blocks.note: second meaning: a speed contest

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an ethnic group of people and also a competition of speed, of which the cycling Tour is an example.

clue.text: What misogynists do, given time and promotion?
